title: Home row review
summary: No new keys. Eight fingers, eight keys, until you stop thinking about any of them.
intro: Nothing new here on purpose. Every reach in the rest of this course starts from the eight keys you already have, and returns to them — so the more automatic they are now, the less work the next twenty-two lessons will be. If you can get through this lesson without looking down once, you are ready to leave the row.
congrats: The home row is yours. From here your fingers start reaching — up a row, down a row — and every one of those reaches ends by coming back to exactly where they are now.

screens.text: Left hand alone, outward and back. Watch that your index finger stays put while the others move.

screens.text: Both hands, mixed. Let it be a little uncomfortable; that is where the learning is.
Pairs that cross between the hands. These are the fastest combinations on a keyboard once your fingers know them.

screens.text: Words again. Read the whole word before your fingers start moving — typing letter by letter is a habit worth not building.

screens.text: A burst of whole words. Speed here comes from not stopping, not from moving faster.
The full row, straight across and back. This is the drill worth repeating on a bad day.
